chunks: And by this chain from Abdullah ibn Hammad from Abdullah ibn Bakr from Humran ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If every angel created by Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, and every prophet sent by Allah, and every truthful one and every martyr interceded for an enemy of ours, the Ahl al-Bayt, so that Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, would take him out of the Fire, Allah would never take him out.
In His Book: 'Staying in it forever.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.نَاصِبٍ: Enemy or foe (specifically of the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Will the enemies of Ahl al-Bayt ever be removed from Hell?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* underscores the severity of enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt by asserting that intercession (*shafa'ah*) by all angels, prophets, and martyrs is ineffective for the *Nasib* (enemies). It highlights a specific Shia theological nuance: while intercession is generally valid, it is suspended for those with entrenched hostility toward the Imams, ensuring their eternal abode in Hell as confirmed by the Quranic phrase 'they will abide therein forever.'
